scope: Proposition 9.2 (Coefficients after compression) of the manuscript “The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free-energy limiting law” (preprints/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-free-energy-limiting-law-September-24-2026/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-free-energy-limiting-law-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 217 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4acb0e456988f38e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 110. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Fix the dyadic restrictions on the base factors and a cut c ≫ w within the region where the small inverse is regular. A sufficiently large fixed separation factor is enough; on size paths require also c ≲ λ. Group base slots into blocks that share their path through c. Their split tree below c is the skeleton, and every designated pair joins distinct blocks. Apply the operator O defined above to the pressure polynomial (E1): it is 1 + ∂θ, with the formal action ∂θ∆ = −∆/6, on a size path, and ∂log λ, holding ∆ fixed, on a direct path. Group the resulting signed allocation coefficients by this skeleton and sum their internal placements within each block. The bound below concerns these differentiated, grouped coefficients. This is a rearrangement of a signed measure. The probabilistic expectations used to evaluate the coefficients remain positive scalar laws on each fixed topology. The spin-model pair tests have been projected to c, or to a neighboring smaller cut, so they depend only on the skeleton and can be kept outside the internal sums. For j = 2, 3, 4, the resulting coefficient, including the skeleton allocation weight, is bounded by O⋄(λc5−j ) Y s skeleton fork dvs/c. (E4) If j = 2, the designated vertices are distinct, and c ≍ w, the bound includes the further factor O⋄(mins rs/c). A factor d or ˙ d may first contribute λc2 to the coefficient, leaving a deterministic factor bounded by the ordinary envelope because r ≲ c. Like b and ḃ, these weights are constant during each internal block sum. Combine contributions only when they multiply the same product of pair tests on the same skeleton. In particular, this combines a repeated pair with the square counterterm. Give such terms the same dyadic restrictions and projection cuts. The cut, shape, and mass coordinates are fixed during coefficient differentiation. Internal summation may then be done before or after that differentiation. The spin tests receive only the formal action on ∆ already specified: project the differentiated polynomial, without differentiating a random test or a projection law.
